a driver failure is recorded with its own code and the phase does not advance
a completed step that fails re-verification is marked failed and the rerun stops there
a crash inside product role creation is recognised on the rerun, never adopted blindly
a crash inside product database creation is recognised on the rerun, never adopted blindly
a crash inside the fleet host's shared pool role creation is recognised on the rerun, never adopted blindly
a crash inside the fleet host's shared pool database creation is recognised on the rerun, never adopted blindly
a same-named role without this installation's provenance is refused and never dropped
a resource that loses its marker after completion fails verification by name
every installation's secrets are distinct, and a copied one is refused as shared
rotating the database credential makes the old password fail before it returns
a crash between ALTER ROLE and the credential swap is finished by the next read, never a lockout
a pending credential whose ALTER never ran is applied on the next read

rotation is refused before resources exist and for a step with no credential
the deployment rotates its own mesh and re-delivers nothing else; the invitation delivers itself
before step 5 exists, a rotated credential is not re-delivered
a step that is not complete cannot rotate, so no invitation is issued ahead of its route
a failed rotation or re-delivery is recorded on the ledger and leaves the step complete
every mutation is attributed on the ledger to whoever asked for it
a ledger with a later step complete while an earlier one is not is refused, never skipped past
a phase another writer moved first is refused, not silently recorded
vector and pg_trgm are created by the cluster administrator, verified on every rerun, and restored after loss
teardown holds the route first, walks steps backwards, withdraws logins, keeps data, and names its residue
teardown of a partial installation tears down only the steps that created something
a teardown failure stops with the tenant still tearing down, and the rerun resumes it
purge needs an installation-issued approval and closed work, drops the databases, and keeps the archive key
bootstrap cannot be observed before the invitation is issued, nor for an unknown tenant
